t: Choose Edges to Maximize Score in a Tree — Tree DP
o: We pick a maximum-weight independent set of **edges** in a rooted tree: no two chosen edges may share a node. This is classic tree DP on 'state of the edge above me'. Walk through example 1: choosing edges (0-1, w=5) and (2-3, w=6) works because they share no node; choosing (0-2, w=10) would block both. Example 2 shows all edges share the root, so we take the single best one, 7. With n up to 1e5 and weights possibly negative, we need an O(n) DFS rather than any exponential enumeration.
k: DP state: whether the edge between a node and its parent is chosen forces which child edges are forbidden.
Negative weights mean 'not choosing' is always allowed, handled naturally by taking maxima with 0 implicitly through child states.
One post-order DFS suffices; recursion depth can hit 1e5, so iterative DFS or increased stack limit matters in practice.

a.i: Define dp[v][0] = best score in v's subtree when the edge (parent(v), v) is NOT chosen, and dp[v][1] = best score when it IS chosen. If the parent edge is chosen, no edge incident to v may be chosen, so every child contributes dp[c][0]. Otherwise each child independently contributes max(dp[c][0], dp[c][1] + w), since choosing edge (v,c) requires c's parent edge chosen. The root has no parent edge, so the answer is dp[root][0].
s: Build children adjacency lists from the parent array.
DFS post-order: compute dp[c] for all children first.
dp[v][1] = sum of dp[c][0]; dp[v][0] = sum of max(dp[c][0], dp[c][1] + w).
a.t: O(n) — each node visited once with constant work per edge.
a.sp: O(n) — adjacency lists, memo, and recursion stack.

w: The two-state formulation is the whole problem; once you fix 'is my parent edge taken', choices across children become independent. Pitfalls: forgetting negative-weight edges (never force a choice), deep recursion causing stack overflow (use iterative DFS or raise limits in Python), and using int instead of 64-bit for sums. Follow-ups: generalize to choosing a matching in an unrooted tree (same DP, root anywhere), or to k-matching constraints.
